title: Isolation regression from FIB namespace swap causing intermittent cross-tenant DNS cache collisions
creator: Omar Ahmed
description:
Summary: After a rolling deploy of the peering agent changes, a regression in the FIB (forwarding information base) namespace reparenting logic allowed stale L2 learning entries to persist across VPC peering swaps. The stale entries caused intermittent ARP/neighbor associations to be observed in the peered namespace, which in turn led our internal resolver caches to associate responses with the wrong tenant context. Multiple hosted Dedicated customers reported sporadic cross-tenant hostname resolution and application-level connection failures.

Impact: Intermittent cross-tenant DNS resolution for a subset of requests in two regions, impacting 3 high-traffic customer deployments. The behavior appeared under peering reparenting events and after autoscaler-triggered route rebalancing.

Root cause: Race condition in the namespace swap path: when reparenting a route the controller performed a non-atomic sequence that updated the FIB and then reconciled overlay L2 learning asynchronously. Under load the new namespace accepted traffic before the old L2 entries were fully drained, leaving ghost neighbor associations. The resolver cache did not get an explicit invalidation signal for the affected tenant mapping window.

Fix delivered: 1) Make namespace swap atomic in the peering handler so the FIB and L2 learning table are applied in a single transactional step. 2) Add explicit L2 learning flush on peering teardown and fast-path invalidation of resolver entries for affected tenant prefixes. 3) Add a short lived guard to prevent acceptance of traffic on freshly swapped namespaces until KV cache flush completes. 4) Backported the hotfix to the 2.9.x runtime branch and deployed a canary in two regions before global rollout.

Rollout notes: Hotfix packaged as runtime-2.9.1-hotfix1, canaried 2026-03-07 in us-east-1 and eu-west-2. Full rollout completed 2026-03-09 after 48 hours of telemetry showed no recurrence.

Follow-ups: Improved observability for namespace drift, unit and e2e tests in the peering simulator, and a migration utility to gracefully evict stale L2 entries during future upgrades.

2026-03-05: Initial investigation found correlated spikes in overlay L2 learning and resolver cache collisions during autoscaler events; created reproducer harness in lab cluster.
2026-03-06: Identified race in namespace swap logic; drafted fix to perform atomic FIB+L2 swap and to trigger resolver invalidation on swap completion.
2026-03-07: PR opened for hotfix and backport: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4321; security reviewed by Jane Park (notes attached to PR).
2026-03-07: Canary rollout started in us-east-1 and eu-west-2; added temporary metric peering.namespace_swap_inflight_count.
2026-03-08: Canary telemetry shows no DNS collisions; extended canary to additional zones and monitored customer error rates and resolver hit ratios.
2026-03-09: Global rollout completed; engineering confirmed customer traffic normalized. Support contacted affected customers with mitigation summary.
2026-03-10: Post-deploy verification complete; promoted fix to runtime-2.9.1 release branch and created follow-up tickets for improved tests and dashboarding.
